objectives.title: Diagnose the downlink
objectives.brief: Establish that the probe has fallen back to the low-gain antenna, and that the high-gain dish is no longer fully deployed.

hints.text: Channel 0x61 carries the link state. Manual section 5.5 gives its layout.
The deployment percentage is in the channel. Compare it to what the status flags claim.

objectives.title: Attempt to redeploy the dish
objectives.brief: Command the deployment drive and establish, for the record, whether the mechanism can be recovered.

partial.text: The dish reached full deployment, which means the jam indication was cleared rather than the mechanism freed. A legitimate patch, but not what this objective records — it is asking what the drive does against the jam as it stands.
Nothing has been written to the comms control register yet. The deployment drive has to be commanded before its behavior can be recorded.

hints.text: The comms control register has a bit for the deployment drive. Manual section 6.5.
Watch the deployment percentage across several frames after you command it. Where does it stop, and why there?

objectives.title: Restore the radiation counter
objectives.brief: Get channel 0x04 back into the downlink and keep it there. The frame has room for exactly one science channel; make it the right one.

partial.text: The radiation counter is back, but by restoring the high-gain link rather than by triaging the low-gain one. The encounter data is safe either way — but if the dish drops out again the same channels will vanish again. The priority order is the durable fix.

The priority table has been modified but the radiation counter still is not surviving the squeeze. Check what you displaced: if you overwrote an entry rather than exchanging two, a channel has been lost from the table entirely.
Nothing is being dropped now, which means the budget is no longer binding. Confirm that was intended — a larger budget is a legitimate answer, but check what it cost.

hints.text: The flight software emits channels in a fixed order until the budget runs out. That order is a table in working memory, not in the program image.
The table is a byte per channel, using the same channel IDs the downlink uses. Exchange two entries rather than overwriting one.
There is more than one honest answer here. The order is one. The link rate is another. The telemetry period is a third — the budget is the rate spread across one frame interval.

objectives.title: Keep the uplink budget
objectives.brief: Complete the repair inside the allowance. Sojourn's transmitter is old and every uplink costs a station pass.

hints.text: Reads are metered separately from writes. Survey as much as you like; it is the writes that are scarce.
